title: Step-1 weight identity P^(1)_j(mu,rho)=a^mu_rho asserted by citation only (prop:transition)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Where.** Proof of `prop:transition` (solution.tex ~lines 957-961): the identity between the Step-1 push-cascade probability and the classical two-line-queue pair weight,
$$P^{(1)}_j(\mu,\rho)=a^\mu_\rho,$$
is asserted **solely** by a one-line citation to [AMW25 Lem 5.4], with no internal verification.

**Why this is a genuine gap.** This identity is load-bearing: it is exactly what converts the three-stage decomposition into the algebraic form
$$P(\mu,\nu)=\sum_{\rho\in S_n(\lambda)}\frac{a^\mu_\rho\,c^\rho_\nu}{e^*_{n-1}}$$
used in `thm:main` to exhibit $(F^*_\mu)_\mu$ as a left 1-eigenvector. By contrast, the *parallel* Step-2 weight identity $P_j P^{(2)}_j(\rho,\nu)=c^\rho_\nu/e^*_{n-1}$ is proved in full, branch-by-branch, in `prop:step2` (Steps A-E): each skip/settle branch is matched to a single sMLQ ball/pairing weight divided by the corresponding factor of $D$. The Step-1 correspondence receives no such treatment. Of the three weight-to-probability correspondences in the paper (bell $P_j$, Step 1, Step 2), Step 1 is the only one that is neither proved internally nor pinned to an exact-statement citation.

**Note this is distinct from q3-8.** q3-8 concerns whether the BDW25a *symbols* $a^\eta_\kappa, c^\kappa_\nu$ (normalization, sign convention, $q=1$ specialization) coincide with the objects given probability meaning here. The present gap is the *dynamical* statement that the actual push-cascade transition probability of `def:chain` Step 1 (activate label $\mu_j$ at site $j$; jump clockwise to the $k$-th weaker particle with probability $t^{k-1}/[m]_t$; cascade until reaching the vacancy; site $j$ becomes the new vacancy) equals the classical two-line-queue pair weight $a^\mu_\rho$ in *this* normalization and site bookkeeping. `prop:step1` rigorously proves Step 1 is *stochastic* (termination, lands on $\{\rho:\rho_j=0\}$, row-sum 1) but says nothing about the *value* of $P^{(1)}_j(\mu,\rho)$.

**Suggested fix.** Supply the Step-1 analogue of `prop:step2`: match the cascade's branching (choosing the $k$-th weaker target with probability $t^{k-1}/[m_i]_t$) term-by-term to the pair weight of the corresponding classical two-line queue, exactly as `prop:step2` Steps B-D do for Step 2. Alternatively, reproduce [AMW25 Lem 5.4] verbatim and verify it states precisely $P^{(1)}_j(\mu,\rho)=a^\mu_\rho$ at the present sites (with activated site $j$ becoming the vacancy) and normalization.
